extracted.intended_audience: historians, archival researchers, editors/translators of Spanish colonial documents; students of Philippine colonial history
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and editorial/ bibliographical notes for preparing, annotating, and publishing editions and translations of 16th–17th century Spanish archival materials relating to the Philippines. Covers manuscript selection, presentation, notation of variants, and explanatory annotation (places, measures, coins).

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of arranging and locating documents in the Sevilla archives
rubrics_metrics.description: The method of arranging and locating documents employed in the Sevilla archives: patronatos (sections) → estantes (shelves) → cajons (cases) → legajos (packets), sometimes further divided into ramos (parts) and números (numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This hierarchical system (patronato → estante → cajon → legajo → ramo/número) allows any document to be easily and accurately located; provide the full pressmark when citing (examples given, e.g., 'Simancas Secular; Audiencia de Filipinas; Cartas y expedientes del gobernador de Filipinas vistas en consejo; años 1567 á 1599; est. 67, caj. 6, leg. 6.').

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer autograph/authoritative MS (Madrid) but incorporate important variants from other copies (Sevilla)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the Madrid MS for the text because it contains Artieda's signature, but incorporate therein all additional matter or important changes found in the Sevilla copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial selection criterion: prefer the manuscript with the author's signature (autograph) as base text, yet collate and incorporate significant readings/insertions from other manuscript witnesses to produce a fuller, more accurate edition; explicitly state the rationale for choosing a base MS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print documents in original language and English translation when available
rubrics_metrics.description: Some documents are printed in both Spanish text and English translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible present bilingual text (original + translation) to enable both source-language fidelity and accessibility; note when only part of a document is printed or when one language version is partial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use brackets for conjectural readings where MS is illegible
rubrics_metrics.description: Words placed in brackets are conjectural readings because the manuscript is illegible in those places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark uncertain or reconstructed readings with square brackets and state that they are conjectural; this signals editorial caution and preserves transparency about uncertainties in the transcription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark and label variant readings between copies (use 'S:' and 'M:')
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpolated matter from the Sevilla copy is shown in brackets, and words altering the sense found in that copy are prefixed with 'S:'; matter in the Madrid copy that gives different meaning is indicated by 'M:'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting a compiled or critical text that draws on multiple manuscript witnesses, explicitly label readings by source (e.g., 'S:' for Sevilla, 'M:' for Madrid) and indicate interpolations and variants in the edition to allow readers to track textual differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full pressmarks and archival provenance for each manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographical data should give the archive, section/patronato, estante/cajon/legajo and other pressmark details so the original manuscripts can be located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include precise archival citations (pressmarks) and note repository names (e.g., Archivo de Indias, Archivo general de Simancas, Museo-Biblioteca de Ultramar) so other researchers can verify or consult originals; list which documents came from which patronato/legajo with examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotate historical place-names with modern identifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide identifications for historical place-names (e.g., Chincheo = modern Chwan-Chow-Foo; Cantun = Canton/Kwang-Chow-Foo; Paquin = Peking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give modern equivalents and variant historical spellings/pronunciations of toponyms to aid comprehension and cross-referencing; include province/region and commonly used modern names when known, and note when identification is uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give modern equivalents and explanations for historical units, coins, and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes supply conversions and explanations (e.g., the escudo ≈ 50.1 US cents, tael ≈ $1.50–$1.68, quintal/arroba definitions, fanega/almude, vara measures, tables of weights).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When historical text uses obsolete units/currency, provide approximate modern equivalents and explanatory tables in notes so readers understand value/weight/volume; explain regional variations where applicable and cite sources for the conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly indicate uncertainty, conjecture, or lacunae in the sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Where readings are doubtful or words are worn off, the editor notes the uncertainty (e.g., 'This word may be "your"; it is uncertain whether the Spanish word is nra or vra.'; 'The words "one thousand" do not appear in the Madrid copy, having probably... been worn off').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag uncertain readings, worn or missing text, and editorial inferences in footnotes or brackets, providing the reason for doubt and the basis for any conjectural restoration; do not present conjectures as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference related documents and secondary literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes direct the reader to related documents and published works (e.g., Retana's Archivo bibliófilo filipino, Philippine Gazetteer, Cartas de Indias, Yule's Cathay, Combés's Hist. de Mindanao).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide bibliographical cross-references and citations to editions, archival documents, and secondary literature so readers can consult fuller accounts and contextual material; cite specific pages/volumes where relevant.
